title: [apm-data] Apply lazy rollover on index template creation

timeline.message:
Apply lazy rollover on index template creation

We should trigger a lazy rollover of existing data streams
regardless of whether the index template is being created
or updated. This ensures that the apm-data plugin will roll
over data streams that were previously using the Fleet
integration package.
timeline.author: Andrew Wilkins

diff.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,54 @@
+---
+setup:
+  - do:
+      cluster.health:
+        wait_for_events: languid
+  - do:
+      indices.put_index_template:
+        name: traces-low-prio
+        body:
+          data_stream: {}
+          index_patterns: ["traces-*"]
+          priority: 1
+
+---
+"Test data stream rollover on template installation":
+  - skip:
+      awaits_fix: "https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/102360"
+
+  # Disable the apm-data plugin and delete the traces-apm@template index
+  # template so traces-low-prio takes effect.
+  - do:
+      cluster.put_settings:
+        body:
+          transient:
+            xpack.apm_data.registry.enabled: false
+  - do:
+      indices.delete_index_template:
+        name: traces-apm@template
+  - do:
+      indices.create_data_stream:
+        name: traces-apm-testing
+  - do:
+      indices.get_data_stream:
+        name: traces-apm-testing
+  - match: {data_streams.0.template: traces-low-prio}
+
+  # Re-enable the apm-data plugin, after which the traces-apm@template
+  # index template should be recreated and trigger a lazy rollover on
+  # the traces-apm-testing data stream.
+  - do:
+      cluster.put_settings:
+        body:
+          transient:
+            xpack.apm_data.registry.enabled: true
+  - do:
+      cluster.health:
+        wait_for_events: languid
+  - do:
+      indices.get_data_stream:
+        name: traces-apm-testing
+  - length: {data_streams: 1}
+  - match: {data_streams.0.template: traces-apm@template}
+  - match: {data_streams.0.rollover_on_write: true}
+

timeline.body:
Trigger a lazy rollover of existing data streams regardless of whether the index template is being created or updated. This ensures that the apm-data plugin will roll over data streams that were previously using the Fleet integration package.

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/116230
Skipped for now like other tests that rely on the templates being installed, as this has proven flaky in CI. I've verified it locally.

timeline.body: This fixes another bug: we were never setting creationCheck to false in the case where there were no data streams to roll over on upgrade. This led to the plugin not recreating templates as intended, as the registry thought template creation was perpetually in-progress.

reply.body: BTW without this change, the existing YAML REST tests would fail with the change to trigger the rollover path on template creation. I've also added a test case for template reinstallation for good measure.
:+1: I like it, thanks for the suggestion. I agree that it's a bit error prone (evidently!) with the way it's spread around at the moment. I will test and push an update shortly.

timeline.body: Hi @axw, I've updated the changelog YAML for you.
It is not clear to me why we are waiting here

reply.body: The intention here is to wait for the apm-data plugin to install the templates. Is that not necessary, or is there a better way?

In general this increases the chances that the templates would be installed before the test runs, but it doesn't guarantee it. So, in this specific case, I do not think it adds anything for two reasons:

1. The only test in this suite disables the apm plugin.
2. You skip the test anyway because we cannot guarantee that the templates will be installed, so why wait?

Fair. The real reason it's there is because I copied another test ;)
I'll remove the setup from this file.

timeline.body: Nice work @axw , in general it looks really good. I added some suggestions, let me know what you think.

timeline.body: IIUC, for other plugins (like otel-data plugin) that are using IndexTemplateRegistry this would be a no-op since there would be no datastreams to apply rollover too -- Is this correct? Maybe we should have a test to assert this behavior as a follow-up i.e. check if `rollover_on_write` flag is `false` for a datastream created after the plugin is installed?

reply.body: I'm not sure I understand the scenario. Do you mean a negative check, verifying something that does not match the index pattern is rolled over? I think the existing `IndexTemplateRegistryTests.testAutomaticRollover` covers that: it creates two logs and one traces data stream, and verifies that only the logs ones are rolled over when updating the logs template.

Not exactly a negative check -- my concern is when plugins operate under normal circumstances then there is no need to rollover on installation. I was thinking of having a test case to cover this scenario to make sure that rollover on installation doesn't break anything for other plugins. Does it make sense?

timeline.body: LGTM, I would still recommend to remove the waiting in the `10_rollover.yml` test, but it's minor. Good work @axw 🚀

timeline.message:
Remove wait_for_events from setup

This doesn't guarantee the templates are set up,
it only increases the chances; and we disable the
plugin at the start of the test anyway.
